Title: Hazy conditions descend on Malaysia again as 31 areas hit ‘Unhealthy’ API
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A total of 31 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 9 am today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, the areas included the Serian Police headquarters in Sarawak with the air pollutant index at 175; Pasir Gudang (170) and Larkin (169) in Johor; Bandaraya Melaka (166); Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (165); Johan Setia, Selangor (163); and Batu Muda in the capital (114).
Thirty areas had a moderate API reading while seven areas had a good API reading.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy and 300 and above, hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Former Felda Investment CEO charged with cheating board over RM500m Jalan Semarak land deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A former chief executive officer of Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC) was charged in the Sessions Court here today with two counts of deceiving the company’s board of directors over the commercial development of Felda land along Jalan Semarak in 2014.
Zaid Abdul Jalil, 56, pleaded not guilty and claimed trial to both charges after they were read out before Sessions Court Judge Rosli Ahmad,
FMT
reported.
On the first count, Zaid is accused of deceiving the FIC board into believing that Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd was qualified for appointment as the project’s master developer, despite knowing the company was only eligible to serve as its master planner.
By misleading the board, he allegedly induced them into approving Synergy Promenade's appointment as the project's master developer during a meeting at Menara Felda on Jan 16, 2014.
On the second count, Zaid is accused of deceiving the FIC board regarding the commercial valuation of 24 lots of Felda land by misrepresenting that a market assessment by Firdaus & Associates Property Professionals Sdn Bhd valued the development at RM330.96 million, when the valuer's actual reported assessment was RM691.7 million.
He is further alleged to have falsely informed the board that the 24 parcels had an indicative value of RM180 million from the Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH), when no such valuation had been provided.
Through these misrepresentations, Zaid allegedly induced the FIC board to accept an offer from Synergy Promenade featuring a proposed minimum guaranteed return of RM500 million or 10 per cent of the gross development value (GDV), whichever was higher.
The alleged offence was committed at Menara Felda on April 29, 2014.
Both charges were framed under Section 417 of the Penal Code for cheating, which carries a penalty of up to five years’ imprisonment, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Radzi Shah Razak proposed bail at RM50,000 for each charge, along with conditions requiring Zaid to surrender his passport and report monthly to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC).
In mitigation, defence counsel Shahrullah Khan appealed for a reduced bail of RM10,000 per charge, citing his client's financial constraints.
Shahrullah said that Zaid had cooperated fully with MACC throughout the investigation and had previously served as a prosecution witness in two major trials, including the graft case involving former Felda chairman Tan Sri Mohd Isa Abdul Samad.
Rosli granted bail at RM60,000 for both charges with one surety, ordered Zaid to surrender his passport to the court pending disposal of the case, and instructed him to report to the MACC office once a month.
The court fixed Oct 29 for case mention.

Title: Marine police, Perhilitan seize RM700,000 worth of protected birds in Terengganu
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Sept 29 — The Kuala Terengganu Region Three Marine Police Force (PPM) and Terengganu Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan) seized more than 50 protected birds and 60 cages worth RM709,950 in an integrated operation near Kampung Binjai Manis, Manir, here Sunday.
PPM Region Three commander ACP Mohd Khairuddin Jamal said all the birds found during the operation yesterday afternoon were protected species under the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716).
He said 38 of the birds were believed to be red-whiskered bulbuls, nine banded pittas and two white-rumped shamas.
“Various other bird species suspected to be protected were also found, including greater leafbirds, orange-bellied flowerpeckers, yellow-bellied sunbirds and red-whiskered bulbuls. Sixty cages were also seized,” he said in a statement yesterday.
The raiding team inspected six houses and arrested a man and two women, aged between 23 and 46, who were suspected of keeping wildlife without a licence from Perhilitan.
“All those detained, together with the exhibits, were taken to the Kuala Terengganu Police Station for further investigation under the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716), including Sections 60(1)(A) and 68(1)(A), subject to the findings of the Perhilitan investigation,” he said.
Khairuddin said the operation involved personnel from the Kuala Terengganu and Tasik Kenyir sectors of the Region Three Marine Police Force, as well as 14 Terengganu Perhilitan officers. — Bernama

Title: Police nab two men ‘chauffeuring’ 690kg of ketum in Toyota Alphard on NSE
Article:
IPOH, Sept 29 — Two local men were arrested after allegedly possessing 690 kilogrammes of ketum leaves in a car at KM371 of the North-South Expressway (PLUS) southbound early yesterday.
Muallim district police chief Supt Khalid Mohamad said the suspects, aged 21 and 31, were arrested by a team from the Highway Patrol (EMPV) Sectors 7 and 8, Northern Zone 4, Bukit Aman Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT) at about 2 am.
He said the two suspects were believed to be runners supplying ketum leaves for the local market.
“An inspection of the Toyota Alphard found 69 black plastic packages containing suspected ketum leaves weighing an estimated 690 kilogrammes, with an estimated market value of RM27,600,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Police also seized the vehicle and a remote-control key for investigation purposes.
Khalid said preliminary checks found that the first suspect had one drug-related record and five criminal records, while the second had two drug-related records and one criminal record.
Both suspects are being detained to assist investigations under Section 30(3) of the Poisons Act 1952. — Bernama

Title: PM lauds Malaysian contingent on best WorldSkills showing since 1995
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated the Malaysian contingent for winning one bronze medal and 13 Medallions for Excellence at the WorldSkills Competition (WSC) Shanghai 2026.
Anwar said the achievement was the national contingent’s best performance in the competition since 1995.
“Congratulations to the 22 youths who demonstrated their prowess and skills in TVET (Technical and Vocational Education and Training), bringing honour to the country.
“Continue to hone your skills and pursue excellence. You are the pride of the nation,” he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
In the same post, the prime minister gave special recognition to Sia Xin Wan, who won a bronze medal in the Software Testing category and received the Best of Nation award.
At WSC Shanghai 2026, the Malaysian contingent of 22 participants competed in 21 skill categories across various technical sectors supervised by the Department of Skills Development and the Ministry of Works.
The tournament ran from Sept 22 to 27 and brought together 1,400 skilled young professionals from 65 countries and regions competing in 64 skill areas. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia launches first phase of Rohingya repatriation to Myanmar
Article:
LUMUT, Sept 29 — Malaysia began repatriating around 1,500 Myanmar nationals on Tuesday, launching the first phase of a return programme that has raised concerns from rights groups.
The group is the first of 5,000 Myanmar nationals Malaysia says have agreed to “voluntary” repatriation from detention centres.
Dozens of buses arrived under police escort at the Majlis Perbandaran Manjung stadium near the Lumut naval base in northwestern Malaysia, AFP correspondents saw.
Reporters were not allowed inside the grounds.
The migrants were expected to be processed before being transported to the nearby naval base and taken to Myanmar by ship.
It was not immediately clear on Tuesday how many in the group were Rohingya, and Malaysian authorities did not divulge the number.
But the persecuted Muslim minority make up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in the country, according to the United Nations.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced in July that Myanmar had agreed to take back 5,000 members of the Rohingya, in a rare repatriation push that has prompted concern from rights groups.
The repatriation plan was announced after authorities detained more than 100 Rohingya who had gathered outside the UN refugee agency’s office in Kuala Lumpur.
The refugees were seeking help after being threatened with eviction from an informal settlement in northern Penang state.
They were later released after officials confirmed they held valid UN documentation.
Myanmar earlier this month pledged “safe and dignified” returns for its citizens displaced abroad, after criticism from the United Nations and rights groups.
Anwar also said he would invite Myanmar’s coup leader-turned-civilian president Min Aung Hlaing for an official visit to help expedite the repatriation process.
Malaysia, which shelters one of Southeast Asia’s biggest refugee populations, is not a signatory to the 1951 Refugee Convention and does not formally recognise refugee status.
AFP fact-checkers have found that Rohingya refugees in Malaysia have been targeted by online disinformation campaigns that rights advocates say are fuelling xenophobia and intimidation.
Many of the Rohingya, a mostly Muslim group, escaped Myanmar during a brutal military crackdown in 2017. — AFP

Title: Felda Investment ex-CEO to face charges today over KLVC project misappropriation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A former chief executive officer (CEO) of Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), investigated for alleged misappropriation involving the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project, is scheduled to be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court today.
A search of the court system showed that the individual is scheduled to appear before Judge Rosli Ahmad at 9 am to face the charges.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), in a media invitation, said it has obtained consent to charge the former CEO today.
On Sept 25, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman reportedly said the individual would face two charges under Section 417 of the Penal Code.
According to Abd Halim, another individual, a former general manager of the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), will face one charge under Section 420 of the Penal Code. The charge is scheduled to be registered in court on Sept 30.
The KLVC investigation is one of seven investigation papers involving Felda and FIC, consisting of six new cases and one reopened case.
The investigations concern asset purchases and investments by Felda and FIC between 2010 and 2020, suspected to involve corruption, misappropriation, and abuse of power. — Bernama

Title: Whistleblowers to get financial rewards for exposing cartels, says MyCC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) will strengthen protection and provide rewards to whistleblowers who provide information on cartel activities or bid-rigging practices, following amendments to the Competition Act 2010 (Act 712) and the Competition Commission Act 2010 (Act 713).
MyCC chief executive officer Datuk Iskandar Ismail said stronger protection was crucial as cartel activities typically occurred secretly and behind the scenes, requiring the cooperation of whistleblowers connected to companies or consumers.
“Previously, protection did exist, but it was insufficient. Now we are further enhancing the protection in addition to providing rewards.
“There were complainants who came forward to provide information previously, but when no reward was given, they left,” he said during the Ruang Bicara programme titled ‘Empowerment of the Business Ecosystem and Consumer Rights through Amendments to Acts 712 and 713’ on Bernama TV yesterday.
He said complainants also faced the risk of losing their jobs if they disclosed confidential company information, which was one of the factors making them reluctant to come forward.
“The complainant said that they were risking themselves to come to MyCC, yet no compensation would be given to them should they lose their job for leaking company secrets,” he said.
According to him, once the amendments are gazetted this year, MyCC will be able to provide more comprehensive protection to individuals who come forward with information.
He said the move would also make it easier for the public, particularly consumers, to lodge complaints regarding anti-competitive practices.
“Now that there is protection, when we enforce these (amendments) this year, it will be easy for everyone, especially consumers, to make complaints.
“At the same time, we will continue to conduct advocacy programmes for consumers every month,” he said.
In this regard, MyCC is inviting individuals or companies with information on cartels to lodge complaints through various channels, including WhatsApp.
Iskandar said the amendments also expanded MyCC’s role in conducting market studies that have a significant impact on the people, including in the digital economy and e-commerce sectors.
According to him, Section 11 of Act 712 grants MyCC the power to conduct market studies on sectors affecting consumers.
He said cooperation with competition agencies in other countries also enabled MyCC to obtain information to ensure the domestic market did not fall victim to anti-competitive practices by international companies. — Bernama

Title: Buying a strata home? The rules that can govern your pets, parking and even your access card
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — As strata properties become an increasingly common choice for homebuyers, owning one involves more than paying a mortgage and maintenance fees.
While a new home may be your own, living in a strata development means not everything is entirely up to you. Residents are expected to abide by rules, commonly known as by-laws, governing how they use their units, facilities and common spaces.
The law behind strata by-laws
For those unfamiliar with them, these rules form part of the broader legal framework governing strata properties in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territory of Labuan under the Strata Management Act 2013 (SMA).
Sarawak has its own Strata Management Ordinance 2019.
Sabah, meanwhile, passed the Building Management Enactment 2026, although it has yet to come into force.
In essence, the SMA provides for the management and maintenance of strata buildings and their common property, while setting out the rights and responsibilities of homeowners and management bodies.
Section 150 empowers the minister, after consultation with the National Council for Local Government, to make regulations for the implementation of the Act, including on the proper maintenance and management of buildings and common property.
What the standard by-laws cover
Because by-laws play a vital role in regulating daily life in a strata community, the Third Schedule of the Strata Management (Maintenance and Management) Regulations 2015 sets out 30 by-laws across eight parts.
Made under the SMA, these by-laws provide a standardised set of rules for strata properties in Peninsular Malaysia and the Federal Territory of Labuan.
They cover everyday issues residents may encounter, including nuisance, pets, vehicles, common facilities, security and unpaid charges.
Under the by-laws governing nuisance, for example, noise from electrical or electronic equipment, appliances or musical instruments used within a parcel or on common property must be kept at a low volume after 11pm to avoid disturbing other proprietors, unless prior written approval has been obtained.
For pet owners, the by-laws prohibit keeping animals in a parcel or on common property if they cause a nuisance or annoyance, pose a risk to the safety or health of other residents, or breach state or local authority laws and regulations.
For vehicles, improperly parked or unauthorised vehicles may be towed or wheel-clamped at the owner’s expense without prior notice.
Vehicle owners must also ensure their alarms are properly maintained to prevent frequent false alarms that could annoy other residents. Management may prohibit a vehicle from entering the development for a specified period if its alarm repeatedly causes a nuisance.
On security, management may require anyone on the common property to identify themselves and, if they refuse and are not a proprietor, require them to leave the common property or development area immediately.
The rules also give management certain powers when charges remain unpaid.
Management may display the names of proprietors with outstanding payments, along with their parcel details and the amount owed, on notice boards in the building. The list must be updated monthly.
It may also, after 14 days have passed from the defaulter receiving the relevant notice and without further notice, deactivate an electromagnetic access device — such as an access card or tag — until the outstanding sum is paid.
Management may also stop or suspend a defaulter from using common facilities or services, including a car park bay on common property designated for the defaulter’s use.
Buildings can set additional rules
The statutory by-laws are not necessarily the end of the story.
Under the SMA, a joint management body or management corporation may, by special resolution, introduce additional by-laws or amend existing additional by-laws, provided they are not inconsistent with the prescribed by-laws.
These may regulate matters including:
safety and security measures;
restrictions on the use of common property;
the keeping of pets;
parking;
floor coverings;
refuse control;
behaviour;
architectural and landscaping guidelines; and
fines of up to RM200 for a proprietor, occupant or invitee who breaches the by-laws.
For example, additional by-laws may introduce more detailed conditions governing pets, such as limits based on size or rules on where animals may be taken, provided those rules are consistent with the statutory by-laws.
They may also introduce stricter security requirements for visitors, such as requiring more detailed identification or documentation than the standard registration process.
That is why two buildings operating under the same statutory framework can still feel quite different from day to day: one may allow motorcycles in visitor bays while another may not; one may specify renovation hours while another imposes broader restrictions.
Can I challenge a by-law?
The short answer is yes.
Additional by-laws must comply with the SMA and cannot be inconsistent with the prescribed statutory by-laws.
The
Strata Management Tribunal
has jurisdiction over certain disputes involving by-laws and resolutions, including claims seeking to revoke amendments to by-laws, while the SMA also allows a management body or parcel owner or proprietor, as applicable, to seek orders from the Tribunal or a court to enforce a by-law, restrain a breach or recover damages arising from one.
Homeowners may also raise concerns over proposed or existing additional by-laws through their development’s general meeting process.

Title: After 70 years together, Dr Mahathir weeps as Dr Hasmah laid to rest
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — After seven decades together, Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today faced one of his most difficult moments as he accompanied his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, to her final resting place.
Dr Mahathir, who used a motorised wheelchair and wore an oxygen tube, remained present throughout the funeral rites as family members gathered to pay their last respects.
A sombre atmosphere marked the proceedings, from the family residence and the paying of last respects and funeral prayers at As-Syarif Mosque, Taman Sungai Besi Indah, to the Pusara Negara (National Cemetery), Precinct 20, Putrajaya.
Looking despondent, the former prime minister was seen gazing blankly for a moment at his wife’s remains while paying his last respects at the mosque before joining the funeral prayers, with thousands of congregants filling the mosque and spilling into the surrounding area.
Upon arriving at Pusara Negara, Tun Dr Mahathir watched as his wife’s remains were taken to the burial plot before she was laid to rest.
From his motorised wheelchair, he observed the burial in a solemn atmosphere as family members stood close by.
Dr Mahathir was seen shedding tears beside his wife’s grave during the final moments, taking a last look at the woman who had shared his life for so many years.
To Malaysians, Dr Mahathir and Dr Siti Hasmah were not merely a former prime minister and his wife. Their warmth and affection for each other, often displayed in public, endeared them to many.
At official events and during more casual appearances, Dr Siti Hasmah was rarely far from her husband’s side, serving as his companion and a pillar of support throughout his life and political career.
The couple’s easy-going nature also frequently drew attention through their jokes, teasing and warm interactions, offering a glimpse into the personal side of two people who spent most of their lives together.
Dr Mahathir and Dr Siti Hasmah tied the knot on August 5, 1956 and last August marked their 70th wedding anniversary.
Over the years, Dr Siti Hasmah was not only a wife and mother to their seven children, but also remained by Dr Mahathir’s side through various phases of life and his long political career.
Dr Siti Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) this morning at the age of 100. — Bernama

Title: Perak seeks RM1.4b in Budget 2027 for key water infrastructure
Article:
IPOH, Sept 28 — Perak is hoping for at least RM1.4 billion in the upcoming Federal Budget to fund key water supply infrastructure, particularly a project to transfer water from Sungai Perak to Bukit Merah to support farmers regularly affected by drought.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said the project was among the state’s priorities submitted by the Perak Economic Planning Unit to the Finance Ministry ahead of the Budget announcement.
“We are currently in the phase of realising the project to transfer water from Sungai Perak to Bukit Merah. If there is surplus water later, only then will we consider selling treated water to Penang.
“This is expected to help meet water needs in Kerian Integrated Green Industrial Park in northern Perak, including for farmers who, as we know, face problems every time there is a drought,” he said.
Saarani said this in a press conference when asked about state government’s wish list ahead of Federal Budget, at the launching of the 2MW Biogas Renewable Energy Plant at the Lahat Sanitary Landfill here.
Saarani said the project was expected to be operational by around 2030 or 2031 if it proceeded according to schedule.
“Hopefully, it will be included in this year’s Budget,” he said.
He said the project would involve two main components, with the first involving infrastructure such as pumps and water tunnels.
“This infrastructure should be funded by the Federal Government through the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry, with the necessary infrastructure works falling under the federal government’s responsibility through National Water Services Commission,” he said.
Saarani said the second component could be financed through Khazanah Air Perak, a consortium involving the state government and a subsidiary of the Perak State Agricultural Development Corporation.
“We can use loans, either from the federal government, through private finance initiative financing or from banks.
“But this can only be done once the infrastructure is in place,” he said.
Saarani said the infrastructure was crucial as the state had already identified the route for transporting water from Sungai Perak.
“We need pumps to draw the water and tunnels to transport it. This is expensive and needs to be started. That is the most important thing for us,” he said.
He said the estimated cost for the infrastructure alone was between RM1.4 billion and RM2 billion, excluding other components of the project.
“The longer we delay, the more expensive the materials will become,” he said.
Meanwhile, Saarani said the state government had also identified several urgent needs involving schools during a recent state development meeting.
He said one of the immediate concerns was the need for additional buildings at existing schools where six- and seven-year-old pupils would be entering Year One simultaneously next year.
“Therefore, there is a need to construct additional buildings,” he said.
Saarani said another concern involved dilapidated school buildings, with the state government receiving complaints from school principals and parent-teacher associations.
“There are many buildings that are already in poor condition, and this is beyond the capacity of the state government,” he said.
He said Perak also needed new schools in areas experiencing rapid development, particularly new growth areas.
“Whenever new development projects take place, there will be a need for new housing areas. Every new housing development should provide a location for a school.
“Schools are very important. We do not want schools operating in two sessions. We want single-session schools and schools that provide a comfortable environment for students to learn,” he said.

Title: Dr Hasmah laid to rest at National Mausoleum as crowd of supporters gather in droves to pay last respects
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 28 — The remains of the late Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali have been laid to rest at the National Mausoleum in Precinct 20, Putrajaya.
The burial was witnessed by droves of supporters, as well as family members and friends who gathered to pay their final respects.
Mourners gathered around the grave as Dr Hasmah’s remains were lowered into the grave, followed by the recitation of the
talqin
, a traditional Islamic rite that reminds the deceased of the tenets of faith, and prayers led by Masjid Putra Grand Imam Muhamad Zakuwa Rodzali.
The state funeral procession continued with the sprinkling of fragrant flower petals and leaves, known as
bunga rampai
, and rose water by former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, Dr Hasmah’s husband, followed by their children and other family members.
Later, the immediate family was presented with the Jalur Gemilang by Official Government Ceremonies Committee chairman Datuk Abd Shukor Mahmood.
Dr Mahathir with family members during the burial. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Apart from family members, close friends and political leaders from across the political divide, members of the public, including families, also attended the state funeral to pay their final respects to Dr Hasmah.
Among those who came to pay their final respects was 77-year-old retired engineer Ismail, who arrived at the Mausoleum grounds at about 3.30pm carrying only an umbrella.
He said he also wanted to offer his condolences to Tun Dr Mahathir, whom he described, together with Dr Hasmah, as leaders who understood the rakyat.
“I used to go against them back when I was young however now that I’m in my 70s, I started to realise how forward minded their vision was.
Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad receives the Jalur Gemilang after his wife, the late Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali, was laid to rest at the National Mausoleum in Precinct 20, Putrajaya, September 28, 2026. — Bernama pic
“They were over ten steps ahead of us and I just realised that recently,” he said.
Retired government servant Datuk Zainal Ayub, 65, meanwhile recalled one of Dr Hasmah’s contributions while she was stationed at the General Hospital in Alor Setar in the 1960s.
He said his late father, who was the Grand Imam in Alor Setar at the time, had been approached by Dr Hasmah to help persuade villagers to give birth at the hospital, as many women then preferred home births and newborn mortality was high.
“Back in those days, a lot of locals preferred to give birth at home and the mortality rate for newborns were high.
“So Tun actually met with my father to ask for his help in advising the villagers there to give birth at the hospital.
“And my father help(ed) her out and he would advise villagers every time during his sermons,” he said.
Retired government servant Datuk Zainal Ayub, 65, recalled one of Dr Hasmah’s contributions while she was stationed at the General Hospital in Alor Setar in the 1960s. — Picture by Arif Zikri
Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia student Ainol Azril Ainol Zaffery, 24, who had never met Dr Hasmah, said he nevertheless regarded her as a national hero for her contributions to the country’s healthcare sector.
He said he was shocked to learn of her death this morning and decided to come to the Mausoleum to pay his respects after finding out the location online.
“I can’t share any personal memories of Tun because I never had the opportunity to meet her.
“But I was amazed about her when I read all the things she did in history books.
“She was one of the First Lady of Malaysia to contribute her medical expertise to the country and I really find that fascinating,” he said.
Retired engineer Ismail, 77, was among those who turned up to pay their final respects, arriving at the Mausoleum grounds at about 3.30pm with only an umbrella in hand. He said he had also come to convey his condolences to Dr Mahathir, whom he regarded, along with Dr Hasmah, as leaders who understood the rakyat. — Picture by Arif Zikri
Meanwhile, 48-year-old Fauzi Sulaiman travelled from Banting with his family to witness the funeral procession.
He said he admired the relationship between Dr Hasmah and Dr Mahathir, describing her as a humble and loyal wife.
“She always kept a low profile despite her great contributions and what I love about her is that she never interfere with her husband works and stayed loyal to him.
“She truly is the backbone of her husband and we’re truly saddened by the news of her passing,” he said.
Although most of the crowd had dispersed by 7pm, a few mourners remained at the Mausoleum to pay their respects.
Dr Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute in Kuala Lumpur this morning at the age of 100.
Members of the Malaysian Armed Forces carry the casket containing the remains of the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali at the As-Syarif Mosque in Seri Kembangan on Sept 28, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa

Title: Bank Negara: Malaysia’s financial markets remain orderly amid global headwinds
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Malaysia’s domestic financial markets continued to adjust in an orderly manner, supported by balanced two-way flows that ensured effective price intermediation among market participants, according to Bank Negara Malaysia’s Financial Markets Committee (FMC).
The “Discussion Summary” of the FMC Meeting 2/2026 revealed that market conditions remained conducive for corporates to raise funds to meet their financing requirements.
“Looking ahead, external factors such as geopolitical uncertainties, oil price volatility and an evolving global interest rate environment remain near-term headwinds for the domestic market. However, members noted that the recent increase in bond yields may present an attractive entry point for foreign investors, given that investor sentiment towards Malaysia continues to be favourable,” the FMC said.
It added that these factors, alongside ongoing measures such as the qualified resident investor programme and engagement with government-linked companies, government-linked investment companies and corporates to repatriate and convert their foreign currency income, are expected to provide continued support for the foreign exchange and bond markets.
The FMC also said recent movements in the domestic financial markets were driven primarily by global factors, particularly developments in the US policy rate.
“Growing prospects of higher US interest rates and the actual realisation of a rate hike by the US Federal Reserve led to a stronger US dollar and higher US Treasury yields. These, in turn, resulted in broad-based adjustments across global markets, including regional currencies and bonds,” it added.
On the currency, it noted that the ringgit moderated in September after remaining largely stable in July and August, while Malaysian Government Securities yields also increased following a prolonged period of relative stability. This came amid a broader repricing of global interest rate expectations and higher global bond yields.
Members of the committee also observed robust interest in corporate bond issuance and increased hedging activity. — Bernama

Title: Hundreds gather at Seri Kembangan mosque to pay final respects to Dr Hasmah
Article:
SERI KEMBANGAN, Sept 28 — Hundreds of mourners gathered at Masjid As-Syarif in Taman Sungai Besi Indah here today to pay their final respects to the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, with the swelling turnout briefly bringing surrounding traffic to a standstill.
Family members, close friends, cross-party political leaders, and members of the public began arriving from 1.15pm, well ahead of the arrival of Dr Hasmah’s remains shortly before 3pm.
Her husband, former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, arrived in a separate vehicle travelling alongside the hearse carrying his wife’s remains.
Traffic police were stationed outside the mosque perimeter to manage the heavy vehicular influx, though surrounding access roads became heavily congested as crowds continued to pour in.
Inside the mosque, the congregation overflowed past the main prayer hall, spilling onto the verandah and crowding the entrance.
Former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad arrives at the As-Syarif Mosque in Seri Kembangan on September 28, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
The gathering drew prominent figures from across the political spectrum, the military, and the Cabinet.
Among those seen paying their respects were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, Bersatu secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and his fiancée Bella Astillah.
Also present were Royal Malaysian Navy Chief Admiral Tan Sri Zulhelmy Ithnain, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, and Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, arrived around 4pm to pay their respects to the bereaved family.
Masjid As-Syarif served as the central venue for all funeral rites, including the final bathing and shrouding of the remains, the public viewing, and the funeral prayers.
The sheer size of the congregation prompted the mosque's imam to organise two separate Asar prayer sessions after the prayer hall reached maximum capacity, ensuring all present could perform their obligatory prayers before proceeding to the funeral prayer for Dr Hasmah.
Members of the Malaysian Armed Forces carry the casket of the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali at the As-Syarif Mosque in Seri Kembangan on September 28, 2026. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Immediately following the funeral prayers, Dr Siti Hasmah’s casket, draped in the national flag, the Jalur Gemilang, was borne out of the mosque by uniformed personnel and transferred into the ceremonial hearse to begin the final journey to the National Mausoleum in Precinct 20, Putrajaya.
Earlier in the day, Anwar announced that Dr Hasmah would be accorded a full state funeral in honour of her pioneering public service and lasting contributions to the nation.
Dr Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) in Kuala Lumpur this morning at the age of 100.
A medical pioneer who was among the earliest Malay women to enter the profession, she dedicated decades of service to improving maternal and child health across rural communities. She married Dr Mahathir in 1956, and they shared seven children.

Title: From violin to rural medicine, 10 things Malaysians may have forgotten about Dr Hasmah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — It is easy to remember Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali through the people and institutions around her: as the wife of Malaysia’s longest-serving prime minister, as a former First Lady, or as the woman who stood beside Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad through decades of public life.
But those descriptions leave out much of the woman herself.
There was the teenager whose schooling was interrupted by the Japanese invasion, the young doctor who worked among rural communities in Kedah, and the woman who maintained interests and a public identity of her own outside politics.
There were also the less expected details: a RM10 payment she refused from a patient’s family, the trust she had to earn from rural villagers, a badminton team she helped establish with other ministers’ wives, and a violin she picked up again in her 80s.
As tributes pour in following her death at 100, here are 10 details that offer a glimpse of the Dr Hasmah that could have been missed by public eyes.
1. She was the only Malay woman in her medical batch
When Dr Hasmah enrolled at the King Edward VII College of Medicine in Singapore, she was the only Malay female student in her batch.
She graduated in 1955, beginning a medical career that would eventually take her from hospital wards in Kuala Lumpur to rural communities in Kedah.
Her time in Singapore was the beginning of a career that would see her become one of the country’s early Malay women doctors and, later, the first woman appointed as a medical officer in Kedah’s Maternal and Child Health Department.
2. She sat her final school exam as the Japanese invasion began
Dr Hasmah was just 15 when she sat her final Senior Cambridge examination at St Mary’s School in Kuala Lumpur in 1941.
She later recalled that on the day of her final paper, bombs were dropped on Singapore and Penang as Japanese forces invaded Malaya.
The invasion brought her schooling to an abrupt end. She did not return to school during the Japanese Occupation, instead remaining at home until the war ended.
She had initially wanted to become a journalist, but her mother’s illness during the occupation helped influence her eventual decision to pursue medicine.
The experience meant that one of the most consequential periods of Dr Hasmah’s life began not in a hospital or in public life, but as a teenager whose education was interrupted by war.
3. She worked with traditional midwives
One of the less remembered parts of her medical career was her work involving traditional birth attendants.
Dr Hasmah recalled working with Unicef to train traditional midwives in cleaner and safer practices.
Women were brought to a training school in Jitra, where they were taught clean midwifery. Those who completed the course received sterilised Unicef birth kits containing items such as scissors, cotton and thread, which they could replenish regularly.
File picture of Datin Seri Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali attending a reception for children with disabilities in Kuala Lumpur, May 31, 1981. — Bernama pic
She also recalled how rural clinics were developed to retrain midwives and create a system in which government midwives could be called in when complications arose.
The work reflected the realities of healthcare in rural Malaysia in the early years after independence, when modern medical facilities were still limited in many communities.
4. She once rejected a RM10 payment from a patient’s family
One of the most revealing stories about Dr Hasmah came from her early medical career.
In a 2016 interview, she recalled that a man offered her RM10 after his wife had given birth and required a blood transfusion.
The blood was supposed to be provided by the hospital without charge.
Dr Hasmah said she initially felt angry, but then sympathised with the man after realising he was poor and believed he needed to pay for the blood.
She returned the money and told him to spend it on food instead.
“I was so angry I cried,” she recalled, adding that the incident made her suspect that some hospital staff had been improperly charging patients for blood.
She described a second incident in which a man offered her RM50 for a medical certificate while she was serving at a station near the Kedah-Thailand border. She reported the incident and became involved in a sting operation.
The stories, she said, were not included in her autobiography because she had forgotten about them when writing it.
5. Her proudest achievement was being accepted by rural Kedah
For all the positions and honours she would later receive, Dr Hasmah once said her proudest achievement in public service was much simpler: being accepted by the people of rural Kedah.
When she first arrived, villagers were suspicious of her. She was from another state, did not understand the local dialect and needed an interpreter to communicate with some of the people she was there to serve.
Over time, that changed.
She recalled how penghulus and other traditional leaders eventually accepted her as one of their own. During durian season, villagers would even pick her up and take her to the estates for what she described as a “nice durian lunch”.
For Dr Hasmah, that acceptance mattered because it showed that the communities she had come to serve trusted her.
It was during this time the infant mortality rate fell dramatically.
She and her team travelled to rural villages to provide treatment, immunisation and health education, at a time when many communities had limited access to healthcare.
By the time she was serving as Kedah’s State Maternal and Child Health Officer, the state’s infant mortality rate had fallen from 75 deaths per 1,000 births to seven per 1,000, according to the Perdana Leadership Foundation.
File picture of Datin Seri Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali opening the 4th Meeting of the Asean Women’s Programme in Kuala Lumpur, February 15, 1985. — Bernama pic
The figure cannot be attributed to one person alone, but it illustrates the scale of the public-health changes taking place during the period in which Dr Hasmah was helping lead maternal and child health efforts in the state.
6. She helped establish a badminton team for ministers’ wives
Badminton was more than a pastime for Dr Hasmah.
In a 2016 interview, she recalled that a sports committee involving ministers’ wives helped establish a badminton team for ministers’ and deputy ministers’ wives in 1985.
The players trained and played competitively, travelling to other states and encouraging the wives of other dignitaries to form their own teams.
Her involvement in badminton continued for decades. She later became a patron of the Badminton Association of Malaysia, while national players from the 1992 Thomas Cup-winning team remembered her as a maternal figure who visited training sessions and encouraged them.
It was a sporting side of Dr Hasmah that rarely featured as prominently as her medical and public-health career.
7. She returned to the violin at 86
Dr Hasmah had played the violin when she was young but stopped at 16 to concentrate on her studies.
Decades later, she picked it up again at the age of 86.
In 2019, at 93, she performed at the Yayasan Universiti Multimedia Charity Hi-Tea, playing Secret Garden’s The Things You Are to Me, Gubahanku and Terkenang-kenang in a 15-minute performance.
A year earlier, she had performed at the Duo Lagenda concert at Istana Budaya, dedicating her violin performance to firefighter Muhammad Adib Mohd Kassim, who had died earlier that month.
The performances offered a glimpse of a side of Dr Hasmah that rarely appeared in official photographs: a musician returning to an old passion well into her later years.
8. She was the first chancellor of Multimedia University
Dr Hasmah spent 15 years as the first chancellor of Multimedia University, from 1997 to 2012.
She acknowledged that she knew little about information technology when she was first appointed to the position.
But she remained closely involved with the university and its students.
She later recalled meeting former MMU students during her travels overseas, saying there was almost always someone who would approach her and tell her they were from MMU.
She also helped establish a Knowledge Endowment Fund to support students and researchers, while MMU later described her as its “Ibu Universiti” — or university mother.
The role gave her another connection with a younger generation, this time outside the medical profession.
9. She was an Umno member — but never held a party position
Despite spending much of her adult life at the centre of Malaysian public life, Dr Hasmah did not hold an official position in Umno.
In a 2015 interview, she said: “I am a member of Umno, but never held any position in Umno.”
She described the prime minister’s wife as an unofficial intermediary between the public and the prime minister, while stressing that she should not make promises involving government decisions or contracts.
But she did occasionally speak publicly on political issues.
In 2015, she accompanied Dr Mahathir to the Bersih 4 rally and described the demonstration as “people’s power”.
In 2017, she also spoke at a women’s rally against what organisers called “toxic politics”, addressing concerns including violence against women and political conduct.
In 2022, she called for more highly qualified and knowledgeable women to enter local politics, arguing that women in politics needed to understand current affairs and what people needed.
10. She was also a teacher — and one of her students carried that work forward
Dr Hasmah’s legacy was not only in the patients she treated, but also in the healthcare workers she taught.
After retiring from government service in 1979, she joined the University of Malaya’s Dental Faculty as a part-time lecturer, continuing until 1981 when Dr Mahathir became prime minister.
She also taught nursing students.
One of them was Matron Fadzilah Abdul Hamid, who went on to spend decades working with women and children affected by HIV.
Fadzilah said Dr Hasmah was among her teachers in nursing school and one of her role models.
“She inspired us with her work, especially when she served the rural community and those in need,” Fadzilah told
Malay Mail
in 2018.
Fadzilah spent 30 years as a Health Ministry nurse, including in rural areas in Selangor, Johor, Pahang and Kuala Lumpur, before overseeing operations and training at Rumah Solehah, a shelter for women and children infected or affected by HIV, from its inception in 1998.
In 2018, she received the Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Award from the Malaysian AIDS Foundation for her contribution towards the HIV/AIDS cause.
That connection offers a different way of looking at Dr Hasmah’s legacy.
It was not only about the patients she treated or the causes she championed, but also the people she taught — some of whom carried that work into the next generation.

Title: Released earlier this year, Federal Court now orders two men back to jail for cannabis trafficking
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 28 — Two men released from prison earlier this year must return to serve the remainder of their original 30-year sentence, after the Federal Court reinstated their convictions for trafficking 264.36 grammes of cannabis.
A three-man bench chaired by Justice Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang ruled that the prosecution had proved beyond reasonable doubt that Azril Azhar Ahmad and Zulfattar Md Ridzuan had trafficked in the drug. Also on the bench were Justices Datuk Lee Swee Seng and Datuk P. Ravinthran.
Delivering the court’s broad grounds, Justice Lee said the Court of Appeal had misdirected itself when it substituted the men’s trafficking convictions with possession, on the grounds that the amount of cannabis seized was only marginally above the statutory threshold for the presumption of trafficking.
“We find there was overwhelming evidence of trafficking as found by the trial court,” he said.
He said the evidence showed that equipment associated with drug trafficking, including a digital weighing scale, plastic packets and a penknife, had been found in the car where the drugs were seized.
Justice Lee said it was never the defence’s case that the drugs were intended for personal consumption, adding that the appellate court had made an assumption based on speculation.
The Federal Court reinstated the 30-year jail term that the High Court had imposed on both men on Oct 20, 2023.
Zulfattar was also ordered to undergo 12 strokes of the rotan, while Azril was exempted from whipping as he had reached the age of 50. The sentence takes effect from Sept 26, 2020, the date of their arrest.
On May 6 last year, the Court of Appeal substituted their trafficking conviction with possession and sentenced both men to eight years’ imprisonment and 10 strokes of the cane, prompting an appeal by the prosecution to the Federal Court.
Azril, 50, and Zulfattar, 44, were released from prison on Feb 23 this year after completing their sentences. Both were present in court today.
The offence took place behind a petrol station in Persiaran Industri Galla, Taman Perindustrian Galla, Seremban, Negeri Sembilan, on Sept 26, 2020.
The two men were also convicted by the same High Court of possessing 8.8 grammes of methamphetamine and each sentenced to five years’ imprisonment and five strokes of the rotan.
The Court of Appeal upheld the jail terms but reduced the caning to three strokes, a decision neither man appealed to the Federal Court.
At today’s proceedings, deputy public prosecutor How Mei Ling appeared for the prosecution.
Azril was represented by lawyers Hasnan Hamzah and Qushwa Hasnan, while Jaspal Singh Mann and Pramjit Kaur appeared for Zulfattar. — Bernama

Title: JPJ cracks down on foreign drivers, 481,119 summonses issued from 2024 to Sept 2026
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Sept 28 — A total of 481,119 summonses were issued by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) against foreign drivers through the special operation codenamed ‘Ops Khas Pemandu Warga Asing’ (PeWA) from 2024 to September this year.
JPJ senior enforcement director Datuk Muhammad Kifli Ma Hassan said the main offences detected were not possessing a Competent Driving Licence, expired Motor Vehicle Licence and no insurance coverage.
He said that out of that total, 183,300 summonses were issued in 2024, followed by 191,676 in 2025 and 106,143 for the period from January to September this year.
“The issue of foreign drivers not only involves enforcement aspects but also includes local employers who hire them without ensuring their qualifications and valid documents, in order to reduce operational costs.
“Employers like that can be considered as colluding or betraying the country. As long as there are parties that collude, this problem will continue. The people need to be aware and responsible for not hiring foreign workers who are not qualified,” he said to Bernama recently.
Muhammad Kifli said that the JPJ has taken a stricter approach in the past three months by taking action against drivers and owners of commercial vehicles, including bringing cases to court without offering a settlement through compound payments for certain cases.
He said that foreigners are not allowed to apply for vocational licences such as Goods Vehicle Licence and Public Service Vehicle Licence, therefore employers need to ensure that lorry or bus drivers meet all the stipulated requirements.
“Employers need to reject the practice of hiring foreign drivers who do not meet the specified qualifications. We will take strict action, including seizing and forfeiting commercial vehicles used in such offences under the Land Public Transport Act 2010,” he said.
He said that since 2024, the JPJ has seized three buses and 147 lorries, while for private vehicles, 3,611 motorcycles have been acted upon, with 2,052 of them being seized. A total of 1,301 cars were also taken action against, including 456 that were seized.
Commenting on the involvement of Myanmar refugees, Muhammad Kifli said his team found that some of them rented motorcycles from locals at rates ranging from RM50 to RM200 per month, depending on the condition of the vehicle, before modifying the motorcycles into tricycles to collect used goods and recyclable materials.
Meanwhile, he denied the viral claim that Myanmar refugees would be allowed to have driving licences, while saying that the JPJ had reported the account spreading the false information to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.
According to him, the JPJ will intensify Ops Pewa nationwide and urge the public to provide relevant information to the authorities to help combat the offense. — Bernama

Title: Civil servant, ex‑CEO plead not guilty to RM18,000 gold mining graft charges
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 28 — A civil servant and a former chief executive officer today pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here to three corruption charges involving RM18,000 in bribes allegedly linked to facilitating gold mining operations in Sabah.
Robert Robin Millip, 60, then assistant director of the minerals division at the Sabah Lands and Surveys Department, is accused of receiving RM18,000 from Chong Tzu Khen, 69, who is charged with giving the bribes.
According to the charges, Chong allegedly gave Robert cash loans of RM10,000 in April 2024, RM3,000 in October 2024 and RM5,000 in October 2025 as an inducement to facilitate the company’s gold mining operations.
The three charges against Chong were framed under Section 17(b) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009 and are punishable under Section 24(1), which provides for a maximum 20-year jail term and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the bribe, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
Robert was separately charged under Section 17(a) of the MACC Act 2009 with corruptly obtaining the three cash loans from Chong to facilitate the company’s gold mining operations, with the same penalties under Section 24(1).
Judge Andi Razalijaya A Dadi granted both men bail of RM8,000 each with two local sureties and ordered them to report to the nearest MACC office once a month, surrender their international passports and obtain court permission before leaving Malaysia.
The court also barred them from interfering with prosecution witnesses and set Oct 27 for case management, while the trial is scheduled for Jan 11 to 13, 2027. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi tells telcos: Rethink diesel gensets, embrace renewables for tower operations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The government has called on telecommunications companies to reassess their reliance on diesel generator sets (gensets) to operate some 60,000 telecommunication towers nationwide, particularly in rural areas.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the large-scale use of fossil fuels to keep telecommunication towers operational needed to be gradually reduced by switching to renewable energy sources, in line with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR).
He said the matter required greater attention given the significant amount of diesel consumed by each tower every month and the large number of towers operating nationwide.
“There are about 60,000 telecommunication towers nationwide. Can you imagine the amount of energy consumed to ensure these 60,000 telecommunication towers remain active and online?
“Therefore, today we have gathered partners whom I regard as strategic partners from various sectors, each of which has an impact on energy consumption. We must collectively look at how a cooperation framework and perhaps incentives can be established to enable them to begin this transition,” he said at the launch of Lestari: Sustainability Framework and Roadmap 2030 (SFR2030) here today.
Fahmi said the development and advancement of the communications industry must go hand in hand with sustainability efforts, including by taking into account the environmental impact of business operations.
In this regard, he said the Lestari strategic framework had been introduced to chart the sustainability direction for the telecommunications, broadcasting, as well as postal and courier sectors towards 2030.
Through the framework, Fahmi said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and industry players aim to sustainably manage 15 million electronic devices by 2030 as part of efforts to help reduce the accumulation of electronic waste in the country.
He said the initiative would also support the circular economy by encouraging the refurbishment and reuse of functional devices, thereby helping to lower the cost of owning smart devices.
The effort was expected to benefit five million people, particularly vulnerable and low-income groups, by expanding access to affordable technology, he added.
The Lestari framework was developed through engagement with 116 participants from 47 organisations and is anchored on three key areas: Climate and Environmental Sustainability; Social Impact and Inclusivity; and Technology and Innovation.
The event also saw the launch of the Net Zero & Circularity Alliance (NZCA), an industry collaboration platform aimed at reducing carbon emissions and expanding e-waste collection in a more organised manner.
Fifteen organisations from various sectors of the digital ecosystem, including CelcomDigi, Maxis, Telekom Malaysia, Astro, Media Prima and Pos Malaysia, signed a pledge in support of Lestari and the NZCA. — Bernama

Title: Sabah police advise against gospel band Israel & New Breed concert over public sensitivities, two reports lodged
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 28 — Sabah police have advised that a band named Israel & New Breed’s planned concert here in October not be held for now, citing public sensitivities and concerns over public order.
Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun said police had received two reports concerning the concert, which has been widely publicised on social media.
“Given the current sensitivities, we will advise that this concert not be held for the time being,” he said, adding that no official application has been made by the concert organisers despite online circulars being publicised including date, venue and ticket prices.
“We advise the state government, which will receive the application, to make a decision and notify the applicant,” he said at a special press conference at the Sabah Police Contingent headquarters here today.
Jauteh also said police had yet to receive any request from the state government for their views on the concert.
He said should a formal application be received, the state government could seek police views before deciding on the matter.
“So far, we have received two police reports. We will continue monitoring the situation and recording statements from certain parties in relation to the concert. We also advise them to take seriously the sensitivities among members of the public at this time,” he said.
He said no investigation paper had been opened over the issue so far, with police currently providing advice based on public reactions and the prevailing situation.
Jauteh said police had also taken note of public reactions concerning confusion over the artiste’s name and allegations about the artiste’s position on Israel.
However, he said the main consideration for police was public sensitivity and maintaining public order.
“What is important here is that we look at public sensitivities and public order.
“We will strive to ensure that any sensitivities that could lead to a situation in which public order is disrupted are addressed, and we will take appropriate action,” he said.
According to the flyers, the concern is scheduled for next month although dates and venue vary slightly on different platforms.
The American praise and worship band, led by a Grammy Award-winning artist named Israel Houghton is on its “Til The Whole World Knows” tour.

Title: Malaysia’s passport now No. 2 globally, sharing silver tier with Singapore
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 28 — The Malaysian passport is now ranked second globally in The Passport Index Global Ranking 2026, rising from third last year.
The Immigration Department said in a social media post that this achievement reflects the strength and international acceptance of the Malaysian passport.
“Based on the ranking, Malaysian passport holders have access to 175 destinations, comprising 129 visa-free destinations and 46 destinations with visa-on-arrival, while 23 destinations require a visa,” according to the post.
Based on data from www.passportindex.org, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) passport holds the top spot in the Passport Power Rank, followed by Singapore and Malaysia in second place.
Meanwhile, Spain’s passport ranks third, while 16 other countries, including Belgium, Denmark, Germany, Sweden, Italy, Switzerland, Austria, and Norway, share fourth place. — Bernama

Title: Lee Chong Wei mourns Dr Hasmah: ‘To us, she was a warrior’
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Badminton legend Datuk Seri Lee Chong Wei has paid tribute to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, remembering her as a “warrior” and a source of affection for the national squad, following her death today at the age of 100.
In a statement, Lee said he was left “frozen” when he received the news this morning, and that his heart felt “truly sad and heavy”.
He recalled speaking to Dr Hasmah in the lead-up to the Malaysia Open earlier this year, when she said she wanted to go to the stadium to support the national players. Lee said her love for badminton “never faded”, and that he had not realised it would be their last conversation.
“To outsiders, Tun was the wife of a former Prime Minister. But to me and the entire national badminton squad, Tun was a warrior, the person we respected most,” he said.
Lee said senior players often recounted Malaysia’s 1992 Thomas Cup victory, in which Dr Hasmah stood by the team as patron, and that she would tear up whenever she spoke of that success.
Over his nearly 20-year career, from his early days in the national squad to competing on the world stage, Lee said she was always present, regardless of whether he won or lost.
He added that she treated the players like her own children and would mediate with “gentleness and wisdom” whenever disagreements arose in the team.
According to Lee, her affection held the squad together and became the “strongest bulwark” for Malaysian badminton.
Lee also noted that Dr Hasmah herself played badminton until the age of 75, saying her passion for the sport inspired him and the whole team.
“Your smile and the warmth of your love will always live on in the court, and in the hearts of all Malaysians,” he said, ending his statement with “Rest in peace, Tun. We will always miss you.”
Dr Hasmah, the wife of former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, died today at the National Heart Institute (IJN) in Kuala Lumpur.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that she would be accorded a state funeral.

Title: Singapore Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong recalls Dr Hasmah’s humour, zest and love for music
Article:
SINGAPORE, Sept 28 — The late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah was a warm and gracious person, full of life, and had a wonderful sense of humour, said Singapore Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong.
Dr Siti Hasmah, wife of former Prime Minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad, passed away at the National Heart Institute (IJN), Kuala Lumpur on Monday morning at the age of 100.
Lee, in expressing his condolences to Dr Mahathir and family, said Dr Siti Hasmah as a doctor had devoted much of her life to improving the health and well-being of Malaysians, particularly women, children, and families.
“Ho Ching and I will remember Tun Siti Hasmah fondly,” he said in his Facebook post on Monday.
Lee also fondly recalled his interaction with Dr Siti Hasmah about her love for music and the violin.
“I remember speaking to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah about her violin performance at the Istana Budaya, when she had played for a good cause.
“She continued performing well into her 90s, including to raise funds for charity. Her zest for life was remarkable,” he said. — Bernama

Title: HEAL 15555 crisis line records 267,873 calls for counselling, intervention since Covid‑19 pandemic
Article:
IPOH, Sept 28 — The National Mental Health Crisis Line (HEAL 15555) has intervened in 518 behavioural crisis cases over the past four years, covering suicidal ideation and suicide attempts.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said that of that figure, 347 cases were of suicidal ideation.
“Some 171 suicide attempt cases were referred through MERS999. With cooperation from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and emergency departments, these individuals were successfully taken to hospital for treatment,” he said.
He said this at a press conference after officiating the national-level launch of World Suicide Prevention Day 2026 at Kolej Poly-Tech MARA here today.
Dzulkefly said the total number of calls received through the line, formerly known as the Psychosocial Support Service Helpline, which was started during the Covid-19 pandemic, stood at 267,873 over the same period.
He said of that total, 220,856 clients (82 per cent) received emotional support assistance, while 47,014 clients (18 per cent) received specific intervention by counselling psychology officers.
He added that the rising number of calls year on year reflects a society starting to open its eyes to the service and to the support system available for those facing mental health issues.
Meanwhile, he said the Ministry of Health (MOH) is working with the Ministry of Education (MOE) to tackle mental health issues among school students that drive suicidal behaviour, including those stemming from stress caused by bullying.
“This includes strengthening counselling services in schools, including screening, referrals and early intervention through the MHPSS (Mental Health and Psychosocial Support) team for individuals, schools or communities affected.
“We are also running the School Health Programme to raise mental health literacy, build healthy coping mechanisms, create an inclusive school environment, and foster inter-agency cooperation, including with PDRM,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Dr Hasmah to be laid to rest beside Endon Mahmood at National Mausoleum
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The remains of the late Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali will be laid to rest beside the tomb of Tun Endon Mahmood, the late wife of Malaysia's fifth prime minister Tun Abdullah Ahmad Badawi.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil disclosed this while sharing the funeral arrangements, after paying his respects at Dr Hasmah's family residence in Seri Kembangan earlier this afternoon.
Her remains were brought to the As-Syarif Mosque in Seri Kembangan for funeral prayers, before being transported to the National Mausoleum in Putrajaya for burial later this evening.
Meanwhile, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi shared that his wife, Datin Seri Hamidah Khamis, had met with Dr Hasmah just last week through their shared ties in the Welfare Association of Wives of Ministers and Deputy Ministers (Bakti).
Zahid said that Dr Hasmah's final conversation with his wife turned deeply spiritual, centring on faith and the afterlife.
“My wife told me that she (Dr Siti Hasmah) spoke a lot about God.
“She spoke a lot about the hereafter. She spoke a lot about the Assembly Place (Padang Mahsyar), as if she already knew that she would be leaving forever," Zahid said.
Dr Hasmah died this morning at the National Heart Institute (IJN) in Kuala Lumpur. She was 100.

Title: Religious teacher pleads not guilty to sexual assault charges involving 16‑year‑old boy in Ipoh
Article:
IPOH, Sept 28 — A religious teacher, known as an ustazah, at a national secondary school was charged at the Sessions Court here today with three counts of physical sexual assault against a 16-year-old male student two years ago.
The accused, Haslina Abu Bakar, 48, however, pleaded not guilty to all charges read before Judge Ainul Sharin Mohamad.
According to the first charge, the accused is alleged to have committed physical sexual assault by kissing the boy on the mouth for sexual purposes in November 2024.
On the second charge, the woman is alleged to have committed the same act by hugging the victim a month later.
On the third charge, she is alleged to have committed physical sexual assault by having the victim touch her chest in November of the same year.
The mother of six is alleged to have committed all the acts in the Islamic Education room of a national secondary school in Kinta at about 3.30pm.
All charges are framed under Sections 14(a) and 14(b) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and caning upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Nor Arfahanim Azureen Arfanuddin did not offer bail on the grounds that the offences are non-bailable, and taking into account the seriousness of the case as the accused was the victim’s teacher, besides the fact that the student no longer attends the same school.
Haslina’s lawyer, Amira Sofea An-Nur Ahmad, however, sought minimum bail, citing that the accused has six children aged between eight and 22 who are still in school and higher learning institutions.
She added that her client suffers from high cholesterol and migraines, her husband has health problems, and she is the family’s main source of income.
Amira Sofea An-Nur also informed the court that the accused is now serving at another school far from the victim, has a good service record as a teacher, is in permanent employment, and has no prior convictions.
The court then allowed the accused bail of RM10,000 with one surety and fixed Oct 28 for mention and submission of documents. — Bernama

Title: Tabung Haji opens Haj appeals Oct 2, earlier start gives pilgrims more prep time
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Tabung Haji (TH) will open appeals for the 1448H/2027 Haj season via the THiJARI application and website from Oct 2, a month earlier than in the previous season.
TH Group managing director and chief executive officer Mustakim Mohamad said the earlier opening would give prospective pilgrims more time to prepare financially, physically and in terms of their knowledge of the Haj.
“The Haj payment for pilgrims selected through the appeal process is the full Haj cost of RM33,300 for the 1448H/2027 season, in line with the concept of istito’ah in fulfilling the obligation to perform the Haj.
“Applications are open to depositors who have at least RM15,000 in their respective TH accounts,” he said in a statement today.
Mustakim said TH had also introduced initiatives such as the #menujuistitoah campaign and the Seruan Istito’ah plan to help depositors prepare for the pilgrimage in a structured manner from an early stage.
Appeals to perform the Haj ahead of a depositor’s scheduled turn will be assessed based on merit criteria and scores, including the length of registration, age, average TH account balance, consistency of recurring savings, frequency of previous appeals and attendance at TH’s Basic Haj Course.
According to the statement, TH will also give priority to appeals involving mahram, companions of selected elderly pilgrims, and companions of selected persons with disabilities (PwD).
“The Haj payment for successful mahram or companion appeals will be based on the rate applicable to the selected pilgrim they are accompanying, according to the B40, M40 or T20 income group.
Meanwhile, prospective pilgrims are also reminded to make the necessary health preparations as approval of their applications is subject to medical screening.
Prospective pilgrims are also advised to equip themselves with sufficient knowledge of Haj rituals by attending TH’s Basic Haj Course, which will be conducted at more than 200 mosques nationwide from Sept 25.
Information, applications and the status of Haj appeals can be accessed through the THiJARI app or website at www.thijari.com.my.
For further information, the public may visit the Tabung Haji website or contact the Tabung Haji Contact Centre at 03-6207 1919. — Bernama

Title: Major city roads, highways to close this weekend for KL Marathon 2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — Motorists are advised to plan ahead as major roads in the city centre and several highways will be closed this weekend for the Standard Chartered Kuala Lumpur Marathon 2026.
On Saturday, eleven roads will close from 5.00am to 10.00am for the IHH 10KM and 5KM races. They include Jalan Raja, Jalan Raja Laut, Jalan Dang Wangi, Jalan Munshi Abdullah, Jalan Ampang, Jalan Sultan Ismail, Jalan P. Ramlee, Jalan Raja Chulan, Jalan Kuching, Jalan Kinabalu and Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin.
Closures on Sunday, October 4, for the full and half marathon are far more extensive, covering 30 road segments.
Jalan Raja and Dataran Merdeka will close from 8.00pm on Friday, 2 October. From 11.00pm on Saturday, Jalan TAR, Jalan Tun Perak, the AKLEH, MRR2 and the northbound DUKE Highway towards Jalan Duta will also shut. The three highways are due to reopen at 11.00am on Sunday.
Most other city roads close at 3.00am on Sunday and reopen in stages between 6.30am and 9.30am. Jalan Sultan Ismail is expected to reopen at 6.30am, Jalan Tunku Abdul Rahman at 9.00am, and Jalan Tun Perak and Jalan Dang Wangi at 9.30am. Jalan Kuching, Bulatan Segambut, Jalan Tun Razak near PWTC, Jalan Kinabalu and Bulatan Dato Onn will stay closed until 11.00am.
Motorists should avoid affected areas where possible and allow extra travel time.

Title: Elderly woman found stabbed to death in Menglembu, daughter with psychiatric history held
Article:
KAMPAR, Sept 28 — An elderly woman was found dead, believed to have been stabbed by her 49-year-old daughter in an incident at Lorong Kledang Utara 6, Taman Wang, Menglembu near Ipoh yesterday.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 70-year-old victim was found with a stab wound to her chest and was believed to have been killed by her daughter, who has a history of mental health treatment.
He said police received a report from the victim’s son-in-law at about 7pm.
“Her mother, who was bedridden and required intensive care, had just been brought home from an old folks’ home in Pusing and was being cared for by her daughter and son-in-law. The daughter also has a history of psychiatric treatment.
“We have detained the suspect, who will be remanded until Oct 4 to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code,” he told a press conference at the Kampar district police headquarters here today.
Mohd Alwi said police also seized a knife believed to have been used in the incident.
In a separate development, Mohd Alwi said the son of a disabled woman who was found dead at her home in Kampung Cheh Kati, Kuala Kangsar on Sept 23 had been sent to Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta for further treatment.
He said the 15-year-old boy had previously been remanded together with his 44-year-old father to assist investigations into the case.
The media previously reported that a 49-year-old woman was found dead, lying in a pool of blood in the living room of her house in the village.
Kuala Kangsar police chief ACP Heisham Harun said police received a report on the incident at 2.38pm after family members found the victim lying face down and unconscious. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorm warning in effect for Pahang, Sarawak and Sabah until 5pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for parts of Pahang, Sarawak, and Sabah, with heavy rain, gusty winds, and lightning expected to persist until 5pm today.
In Peninsular Malaysia, adverse weather conditions are forecast across three districts in Pahang, namely Cameron Highlands, Raub, and Bentong.
In Sarawak, the alert covers the Bintulu division (Bintulu and Sebauh), Miri, and the Limbang division.
In Sabah, the warning covers a wider area, encompassing Tawau, the Sandakan division (Tongod, Telupid, Kinabatangan, and Sandakan), the Interior division (Sook, Keningau, Tambunan, Membakut, and Pensiangan), alongside the West Coast division and Kudat.
MetMalaysia explained that a thunderstorm warning is triggered when atmospheric indicators point to impending storms with rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour, or when precipitation is expected to last for more than an hour.
These alerts serve as short-term advisories and remain valid for a maximum duration of six hours from the time of issuance.
Residents in the affected areas are advised to stay vigilant, avoid open fields, steer clear of large trees and unstable structures, and prepare for potential flash floods, especially in low-lying zones and near slopes. Motorists have been urged to exercise extra caution on the road due to reduced visibility and slippery surfaces during heavy downpours.
